chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from Khaleylan ibn Hisham who said:

I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! With us there is a drink called Al-Mayba, made from quince. We peel it and place it in water, then we take the juice and cook it until one-third remains. Then we pound that quince and take its water. Then we take the water of this reduced juice and this quince, and we cast musk, cloves, saffron, and honey into it, and cook it until two-thirds evaporates and one-third remains. Is it permissible to drink it?' So he wrote: 'There is no problem with it, as long as it has not changed.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a quince-based drink to be considered halal according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *istishab* (presumption of permissibility) applied to traditional beverages, where the base state of quince and water is considered pure unless proven otherwise. The Imam’s condition 'ما لم يتغير' (as long as it does not change) refers specifically to the change in state leading to intoxication (*khamr*), rather than mere cooking or fermentation, reflecting the nuanced distinction between mild consumption and intoxication in Shia fiqh. It highlights the practical application of purity laws to pre-Islamic Arabian culinary traditions, validating local customs provided they remain within halal boundaries.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ibrahim Bin Mahziyar, from Khaleylan Bin Hisham who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassanasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! With us there is a drink called Al-Mayba made out of the quince. So it is peeled and placed in the water, then we take to the (grape) juice, so we cook it upon the third, then we pound that quince and we take its water. Then we take to the water of this third, and this quince, so we cast the musk in it, and the condiment, and the saffron, and the honey, so we cook it until two-thirds of it evaporates and there remains its third. Is it Permissible to drink it?’ So heasws wrote: ‘There is no problem with it for as long as it has not changed’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar from Khalilan ibn Hisham who has said the following:

“I once wrote to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, in our area there is a drink called al-Myabeh which is taken from quince which is peeled then is placed in water. Juice (grape juice) then is boiled until one-third (is left), then the quince is crushed. Its juice then is taken. Then the one-third water and quince, musk, spices and condiment, saffron and honey are cooked until its two-thirds are evaporated and only one-third is left; if it is lawful to drink it. He (the Imam) wrote, ‘It is not unlawful as long as it is not changed. 5 ”
